---
title: "Data Notes"
---

All data on this site comes from public sources — the Census Bureau (American Community Survey, decennial census, Population Estimates Program, Building Permits Survey), the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and TIGER/Line boundary files via `tigris`. No licensed or proprietary data (MLS, CoStar) is used.

## Chesterfield one-pager: pay and affordability

The [Chesterfield one-pager](chesterfield-onepager.qmd) uses starting pay from the county's own postings and class specifications and from Chesterfield County Public Schools' February 3, 2026 compensation presentation, all retrieved November 23, 2026. Each pay figure carries its source, date and a status: *current* (latest figure confirmed in the source), *proposed* (not confirmed adopted) or *stale* (predates the current fiscal year). Hourly rates are annualized at 2,080 hours. Affordable rent is 30% of gross income. Affordable home price assumes the Freddie Mac 30-year rate for the week of November 12, 2026, 5% down, the county's $0.89 per $100 real estate tax rate, and insurance and mortgage insurance. Median rent and home value are 2020-2024 ACS 5-year estimates; the HUD 80% income limit is FY2026 for the Richmond HUD Metro FMR Area. The data are in `data-out/chesterfield_pay.csv` and `data-out/chesterfield_onepager.csv`.
The one-pager also uses Chesterfield-only ACS tables on household size (B25009), bedrooms (B25042), householder age (B25007) and cost burden by householder age (B25072, B25093), the 2020-2024 PUMS income-band estimates behind the profiles page, and Census population estimates. Cost-burdened means 30% or more of income goes to housing. The data are in `data-out/chesterfield_hh_size.csv`, `chesterfield_bedrooms.csv`, `chesterfield_hh_age.csv` and `chesterfield_burden_age.csv`.


*Full methodology to be written alongside each page — see [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md) for the internal version of these notes.*
